name: select_by_tag
description: select.byTag region parity. The reference offers no command that turns a tag into a polygon selection -- measured: two of the three ids the audit named do not exist, and the third selects the TAG rather than the polygons and does not drive polygon commands. What IS measurable, and what this fixture freezes, is the REGION: after tagging two selected faces of the unit cube, exactly those two carry the tag and the other four read the default. Our select.byTag must hand that same region back.
source: LIVE-CAPTURED from the reference editor, driven headlessly through its command line: a unit box with one segment per axis, the +Y and +Z faces selected by centroid predicate, a named surface assigned to them, then every polygon's material tag read back off the geometry. Measured partition: (0,0.5,0) and (0,0,0.5) carry the named tag, the other four read as the default.

provenance.notes: The tag IDENTITY differs by construction and is not part of the claim: the capture names surfaces ('Red'), we index them (materialId 1). The claim is the SET of polygons. Also measured and deliberately NOT adopted: the captured material command retags the WHOLE MESH when nothing is selected, where mesh.setMaterial is a no-op -- see the task file.

parameters.notes: drive record read from tests/fixtures/select_by_tag.json:93,192; Re-projection of the fixture's OWN `input` steps; the generic extractor misses them only because they sit under `input` as `{endpoint: command, body:{id,params}}` rather than under `op`. SPLIT: the `select` steps (the two seed faces and the deliberate drop before the read-back) and `mesh.setMaterial materialId:1` are the STAND -- they build the tagged region the query is pointed at; the only operation under test is `select.byTag`, whose `id` argument IS a parameter and is recorded at both 1 and 0.

cases.name: region_round_trip
cases.description: Tag two faces, drop the selection, ask for the tag back: the same two faces return. The drop is the whole point -- without it the command could pass by doing nothing at all.

cases.name: default_region_is_the_complement
cases.description: The untagged four are a region too -- the reference reads them as the 'Default' tag, which is our material 0. Asserting it keeps 'select everything' from passing the case above.
